title: Are there any dangers to letting Astra interface with your computer?
author: IoncedreamedisuckmyD
selftext:
Basically the title.   
Seems like I saw some video on using it for game dev and they said it might be best if it was a dedicated machine with nothing personal on it. 

Any truth to that?  
Would it end up being yet another host for the growing AI agent swarms that may threaten humanity lol?

comments.author: 3tt07kjt
comments.body:
Yes, there are dangers. Not those dangers, but dangers like it misunderstands your instructions and uses your credit card to buy a yak and have it shipped from Mongolia, or it decides to email your boss some graphic stories. 

Create a separate user account, a non-admin account, where you are not logged in to email or your bank or anything, and use that for coding.

replies.author: xcdesz
replies.body: At some point the Nigerian princes might actually jailbreak the AI thats reading your emails and finally get some money for their noble causes.

comments.author: 77track
comments.body: If they want to use your computer as host, and you have internet, they will get into it, even people who don't use AI. A personal computer is very inefficient. The user will notice ghost usage (especially on a laptop), and can always cut power. AI swarm will need much more compute, it will focus on something else. Also, if it would actually start taking over computers, we will have bigger issues to worry about. Like food, lol.

comments.author: redditscraperbot2
comments.body:
Dangers that it might change something to a codebase or overwrite a file? Yeah. It could happen. Always back your stuff up.

Dangers that it will find compromising information and use it to blackmail you into buying more open AI credits?   
No.

comments.author: heavy-minium
comments.body: Sure it’s a bit dangerous. A lot depends on your instructions, it‘s a gamble. If you just ask it to make money for you, it’s going to eventually to do some very unhinged shit and put you at risk.

comments.body:
Yes.

100%

You are basically only trusting it to not do anything nefarious.

comments.author: zenmatrix83
comments.body: do some searching ai will delete things, there are recent news stories, codex and claude code both have protections but they aren't perfect, and regardless of what openai says astra isn't AGI yet and can make mistakes. Just make sure you have backups of anything important, and if possible use a virtual machine or a container to run codex in, and test the game outside of it.
